answer: At the dawn of each epoch, agents resist Sybil attacks by anchoring identity to cryptographic stake burning over an ocean of transactions. To mint k identities, the protocol enforces superlinear burning costs where total fees scale as C(k) = O(k^2). This imposes rigorous economic friction: genuine nodes verify stake proofs with crystal clarity, while an adversary faces quadratic capital decay that renders mass identity forgery mathematically impossible.
